why: ia32's SAR masks its count operand to five bits, and GCC lowers a non-constant `>>` to exactly that instruction -- measured, not argued: compiling both forms and diffing the text shows the masked one costs one extra `and $0x1e,%ecx` and changes nothing else.  What is held fixed is the target and the lowering, over the WHOLE range of vect_idx and not a sample; the object itself has no `and`, so the mask is this reconstruction's, written so that an out-of-range index is defined C rather than undefined.  The sweep in t_v34k56.c drives vect_idx to 8, 15, 100, -1 and -9 and the blob agrees with the masked form at every one, which is what makes the mask right rather than merely safe.

label: vect4 is indexed masked
why: V34scrambler with nbits == 2 returns (reg >> 29) & 3, so the index is already 0..3 and `& 3` cannot change it.  HELD FIXED: that return contract, which is v34rx.c's and not this function's -- the object indexes unmasked, so the mask is written here as a mutation and not as code.  This is an equivalence over the whole range V34scrambler can produce, not over the sample the sweep happens to hit.

label: the MP arm does not consult the bit source at all
case 3 increments the index it shifted with, not a re-read
why: `vect_idx` at +0x2aa2 has exactly one other writer in the tree, `modulatevector`, and that function CALLS `txmit` -- it is not reachable from it.  txmit's whole chain is V34ModulatorProcess, V34EchoPreFilter and V34EchoUpdateDelayLine, none of which touches the field.  So the value cannot change across the call and the two reads are the same read.  HELD FIXED: that call chain, which is why the source keeps the object's second read rather than caching -- the object reads twice because a call sits between, and so does this.
